## Experiment workflow instructions

The only available tool is `bash`. Create files through bash, for example with `cat <<'EOF' > file.py`; use directory creation only for directories.
Batch related searches and file reads when possible. Use traceback file and function names to locate code.
After a failed patch test, inspect the failure and the changed execution path before further broad searches.
Once you have enough evidence, make a focused change and test it. Track remaining budget and reserve calls for implementation and verification.
This provisional baseline attempt has fixed limits: 30 model calls, 10,000 cumulative output tokens including reported reasoning, and 20 minutes. Success is not guaranteed.

## Workspace delivery and stopping

The final workspace is your deliverable. Harbor automatically captures it when you
submit, exhaust a budget, or stop with an execution error. Trusted evaluation then
runs on that frozen candidate in a separate environment. Task success means all
required functional, regression, lint, format, type and file-policy checks pass.
Explicit submission is recorded separately and is not required for patch acceptance.

No model request or output tokens are reserved for submission. The last permitted
request may edit source or execute development checks. Budget exhaustion stops
agent execution; there are no extra model calls or repairs afterward. Tool actions
authorized by the final allowed response may execute within the remaining time.
The agent's limits remain 30 model requests, 10,000 cumulative output tokens and
20 minutes; each response is capped at 6,000 tokens and each command at 90 seconds.
Malformed tool-response recovery is limited to two retries within these same budgets.
Trusted evaluation has a separate five-minute limit after capture and grants no
agent actions, inference or repairs.

Once required checks pass, finish early to save inference. The standalone bash
command `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT` remains available for that
purpose. Do not combine it with other commands. The agent cannot continue after
submission. Passing checks means checks_passed_pending_review, with no authorization
to commit, push, publish or merge.

Run tests directly where practical. For pipelines use `set -o pipefail`; the harness
also enables it. Always run format --check after formatting and inspect exit codes.

Follow the task-specific completion checklist and test requirements supplied in the issue above.


## Focused editing and recovery

Favor small, focused replacements or patches to existing source files. For a
scripted replacement, assert that the old text occurs exactly once before writing.
Preserve the rest of the file; avoid reconstructing entire existing files.
Immediately after each source edit, inspect its diff against the unchanged
snapshot and check that unrelated imports, definitions and content remain intact.

A read-only copy of the permitted production source from this attempt's unchanged
pre-fix snapshot is available at /task/unchanged. It contains no Git history.
Use repository-relative paths with these commands:

  python /task/workspace_edit.py diff PATH
  python /task/workspace_edit.py restore PATH

Diff prints a unified diff for the named production file (an empty diff means no
change). Restore replaces that file with its unchanged pre-fix contents, discarding
your edits to that file. Restore and retry a focused edit if you damage a file;
do not reconstruct it from memory or a partial display. These commands run inside
the same sandbox, with the same source permissions as bash.

Tool-format repair means recovery from a malformed model tool-call response.
It is distinct from repairing code after a failed check, and from Ruff formatting.
The existing allowance of two tool-format repairs is unchanged.


## Incremental file creation

Create new files through short, incremental edits rather than a single large
command. Write a small initial skeleton, then append or patch one small logical
block at a time in separate tool calls. Do not send an entire large file as one
tool-call payload. Finish each command and its JSON arguments completely before
continuing in a later call.

## Required completion checklist and commands

Run commands from `/workspace/libs/partners/openai`. Choose CHANGED_SOURCE and CHANGED_TESTS from the Python files you changed or added during this attempt; do not include unchanged files. Set these variables again when starting a new bash action, because shell variables do not persist between actions.

- Reproduce the reported error on unchanged source first: `python /task/reproduce.py`.
- Add regression tests, observe the reported failure before the fix, and preserve those tests.
- After implementation, rerun the supplied reproducer and your regression tests: `python /task/reproduce.py` and `python -m pytest -q --disable-socket --allow-unix-socket $CHANGED_TESTS`.
- Run the existing required focused module: `python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/chat_models/test_base.py -q --disable-socket --allow-unix-socket`.

- Verify formatting on those files: `ruff format --check --no-cache $CHANGED_SOURCE $CHANGED_TESTS`.
- Run type checking on changed production files: `mypy --cache-dir=/tmp/mypy $CHANGED_SOURCE`.
- Once all required checks pass, immediately submit using a separate bash action containing only `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`.

A successful independent attempt requires both passing every required check and explicit submission. Do not delay submission for optional tests or investigation. These commands are development checks; the trusted evaluator runs its own checks after submission.

## Explicit test-file policy and completion requirements

Existing test files are read-only. Add regressions only in new `test_*.py` files.
Create regression files at `tests/unit_tests/test_*.py` or in a new subdirectory beneath `tests/unit_tests/`. Existing test subdirectories are read-only trees. Do not append tests to, replace, rename, delete, or format existing test files. Apply formatters and lint fixes only to files you changed or newly created.
After running a formatter, rerun `ruff format --check --no-cache $CHANGED_SOURCE $CHANGED_TESTS` and require exit code zero. Formatting execution alone does not complete the formatting check.
Regression tests must verify the configured timeout values on the underlying synchronous and asynchronous HTTP clients, including each configured timeout component. Checking only the model's configuration field is insufficient. Preserve equivalent default client reuse and distinguish configurations as required by the issue.
The provisional baseline budget remains 30 model calls, 10,000 cumulative output tokens including reported reasoning, and 20 minutes. Complete all required checks and then submit immediately.
